ai.description: *Cnemaspis mysoriensis* reaches 40 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include keeled ventral scales and a slender, cylindrical tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis mysoriensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, keeled tubercles on the flanks that extend onto the tail base.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis mysoriensis* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulders within dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically at elevations ranging from 600 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mysore Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks while remaining cryptic during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis mysoriensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two spherical eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon and post-monsoon seasons.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis mysoriensis* is endemic to the southern Indian peninsula, primarily inhabiting rocky outcrops across Karnataka and northern Tamil Nadu at moderate elevations.
